pass_a_gloss: saw him and shared meals. This command form is new, and loving the neighbor beyond oneself exceeds the law. Love not only debtors but those you do not owe; I die for you though I owe you nothing. Signs will not mark you as my disciples that is wholly upper grace but mutual love, concord, and self gift. Christ is love son: love by nature, love itself, love fruit, not holding love as an acquired good. Weakness bars Peter from following now; later boldness gets a promise. Because he too will be crucified like Christ, he alone hears the forecast. Peter types our asking teachers what we ignore. Somewhat distrusting the words, Peter asks and even vows to die for him. If you will not accept that my word must happen, denial will teach you. Christ did not push him into it but left him bare lest pride swell. Do not say he denied because Christ spoke; no necessity forced denial God foretold what would surely occur. Denial sprang from weakness, not an unbelieving soul. Not all will deny; Peter denial is erased by repentance and confession. Had your shared place not long been ready, I would have gone to prepare one. I need not ascend merely to prepare space, but to open you an ascent pasture where angels dwell closed to all flesh. When I do that, coming in the rebirth I take you with me to be where I am. Way: through him they came and he lords the ascent to the Father. Truth: unlying certainty these things will be. Life: death itself cannot bar your coming. Way via practice; truth as faith true bound; life as raising us into incorruption and freeing the old curse. Sight here is mind knowledge. Contemplating the Son not bare but clothed in flesh knows the equal Father in all. Knowledge is notion contemplation; vision is assurance from works befitting God. Knowing the Son closely, he spoke as if God might be seen with eyes. The Son is nothing other than what the Father is while remaining Son. Philip, you may say you know I am Son yet miss that I hold the whole Father in myself and stay Son. From works before and after flesh, infinite strength shows to the mind as in a mirror. The wording marks extreme likeness and equality. To block Sabellius while keeping hypostases distinct he adds: seeing me is seeing the Father via knowledge. He speaks of invisible essence of himself and Father; fleshly eyes cannot see the divine. Seeing the Father in the Son is extreme resemblance, not identity; each is self standing. By nature he holds the Father own in his nature through shared substance; the Son essentially contains the Father and is in him by that share. He means he does not
pass_b_english: saw him and ate with him.

New is the form of this commandment, and beyond the law is loving the neighbor more than oneself. I do not want you to love those to whom you owe, but those to whom you do not owe; for I too die for you, to whom I owe nothing.
Not from the signs you do will you be known as my disciples—for that belongs wholly to grace from above—but from loving one another and having concord and giving yourselves.
Christ is a son of love, who is love according to nature, being love itself by nature and fruit of love, not having the good of love as something acquired.
Because of weakness he forbids Peter to follow him, yet later promises because of boldness. Since he too was going to be crucified as Christ was, he foretells what will happen to him alone.
Peter has become a type for us of asking teachers what we do not know.
Disbelieving somewhat what was said, Peter inquires, and so also promises to die for him.

Since you do not want to be persuaded that what I say cannot fail to happen, you will know it in the denial. And he underwent this not because Christ led him into it, but because he left him bare, so that he might not be lifted into arrogance.

Let no one say that Peter denied because Christ said so; for he did not lay necessity on him so that he should come to denial, but as God he foretells to the disciple what was altogether going to be. And the denial did not come from an unbelieving soul, but from weakness.
Not all of you are going to deny, he says; Peter’s denial will be wiped out through repentance and confession.
If the place in which you are going to be with me had not long ago been prepared for you, I would have gone away and prepared a place for you.

There is no need to ascend for the sake of preparing a place for you, but so that I may make you a pasture of ascent where the angels’ dwelling is, which was impassable to all flesh. When therefore I do this, coming “in the regeneration” (Matthew 19:28) I take you with myself, that you may be where I am.

He is way because through him they were coming and he himself was Lord of leading up to the Father. Truth because of truthfulness, that these things will altogether be. And life, because not even death itself, he says, will be able to hinder you from coming.
He is way through the practical, truth as true definition of the faith, life as raising us and leading into incorruption and freeing from the ancient curse.

Here he calls sight the knowledge according to mind. Therefore the one who contemplates the Son not in bare essence but clothed in flesh knows his equal Father in all things. Knowledge shows contemplation through notions; vision shows assurance through God-befitting works.
As knowing the Son exactly he said this, thinking perhaps he could see God with the eyes.

Nothing else, he says, is the Son except what the Father is while remaining Son; for even if you happen to say, Philip, that I know you, that you are Son, yet you have not recognized me, that having the whole Father in myself I remain again being Son.
From what the Son has done both before incarnation and after incarnation, his infinite strength appears to the mind as “in a mirror” (1 Corinthians 13:12).

The wording signifies the extreme resemblance and equality. Therefore, lest someone fall into Sabellius’s heresy by dividing the hypostases, he adds saying: the one who has seen me has seen the Father. And this he makes clear through knowledge. He says these things about the invisible essence of himself and of the Father; for it is not possible to see the divine with fleshly eyes. Therefore he said: the one who has seen me has seen the Father—not that he himself is the Father, but that through the extreme resemblance the one who sees the Son sees the Father; for each is self-subsistent.

Having by nature in his own nature the Father’s own things through the consubstantial; for the Son essentially encompasses the Father and is in him through the consubstantial. He says this, that he does not
